critical_code_review_comments: _build_directional_liq_fallback() uses voting system: market.trend (+1/-1), market.htf_trend (+1/-1), orderflow.bullish_ratio/bearish_ratio (+1 each if >= 1.03)
Tie-breaker rule: if bullish_votes == bearish_votes, returns neutral analysis (no target)
Target distance calculation: max(atr * 1.8, current_price * 0.004) - ensures minimum 0.4% distance from price
Fallback ATR: when atr_val <= 0, uses current_price * 0.008 (0.8% of price)
Bearish target has floor at 0.0: max(current_price - distance, 0.0)
Fallback is used in both _manage_positions (line 374-375) and _analyze_symbol (line 506-508)
_analyze_symbol still has final guard at line 510-511: returns EntrySignal() if target_level <= 0 after all fallbacks
Priority chain preserved: live events -> synthetic heatmap -> directional fallback

context_for_next_testing_agent: All directional heatmap fallback features verified. The fallback creates a target when: (1) live liquidation events produce no target, (2) synthetic heatmap from price action also fails. Direction is determined by voting: trend (+1/-1), htf_trend (+1/-1), orderflow ratio (bullish/bearish +1 if >= 1.03). If votes tie, returns neutral (no trade). This should remove the final no-trade choke point for eligible symbols. No live network testing performed per instructions.
rca_of_the_issue: Previous choke point: _analyze_symbol would return no signal if heatmap target stayed zero even after synthetic fallback. Root cause was that low-price symbols with no liquidation events and flat candle patterns could produce zero targets from both live and synthetic heatmaps. Mitigation: Main agent added _build_directional_liq_fallback() which creates a directional target based on market trend + HTF trend + orderflow consensus when both heatmap sources fail.
